Figital LABS

Mascot options · round 3 · with market check

Ten object mascots, checked against the market

Every option is drawn as one complete character in the same style, so you compare ideas rather than drawing quality. For each, two agents searched for brands already using the object, the name, and any cultural or political meaning, on 14 October 2026.

What the check found

The objects are open

None of the ten objects is an established brand mascot. No Indian healthtech (Practo, PharmEasy, Tata 1mg, Apollo 24|7, MediBuddy) has a character mascot at all; PharmEasy uses a celebrity.

The names are the problem

Seven of the ten names clash: with a direct competitor (Nudge AI), a health app (Disha), a clinical term (Baton), a political symbol (lantern), or a bad meaning (Gaanth = lump, Dabba = junk or illegal trading).

So choose in two steps

Pick the object first, then name it separately and run a trademark search. The working names below are only labels.

Every option

Shortlist

Nudge

Sticky note

The note every nurse station and billing desk runs on. It sticks to a task until its checkbox is ticked.

Checkbox ticks itself to celebrate · folded corner flicks like an ear · peels off a mini note to present.

Object used elsewhere?
Clear. No brand uses a recurring sticky-note character. 3M's Post-it has none; a 2019 3M ad turned notes into an octopus once.
Name risk
High. Nudge AI (US) sells an AI clinical scribe and an AI billing auditor, the same products as Figital. Healthkind Nudge (Canada) automates patient messages.
Watch
Microsoft's Clippy, the reviled Office paperclip helper, is the cautionary tale for any office-object assistant.

Sources: Nudge AI · Healthkind Nudge · Clippy

Keep the sticky note, change the name.

Shortlist

Chitthi

Letter

A letter that always reaches the right desk. Fits how NotedAI routes each complaint to its department.

Flap opens to talk · folds into a paper plane to travel · the teal seal is its “done” mark.

Object used elsewhere?
Mostly clear. No major brand uses an envelope character. India Post ran a mascot design contest (July–August 2026) and the winner isn't public yet; a letter design there would clash.
Name risk
Low. Only small pen-pal projects (Chitthi Exchange). Nothing in health or software.
Watch
Watch the India Post mascot result before committing.

Sources: India Post contest · Chitthi Exchange

Warm, Indian and open, pending India Post.

Shortlist

Dhaaga

Thread spool

A spool whose thread runs through every step of the patient journey, tying OP to IP.

Thread draws a path to point · winds itself up to think · ties a neat bow to celebrate.

Object used elsewhere?
Clear. No spool mascot found in any industry.
Name risk
Low in health. Used by Indian fashion and craft brands (Dhaaga Life, chikankari labels) and the film Sui Dhaaga; nothing in health or software.
Watch
Thread is sacred in Hinduism (janeu, kalava). Keep it teal, never red-and-yellow, and never worn on the wrist.

Sources: Sui Dhaaga · Janeu

Open in health and tech; design around the sacred-thread look.

Maybe

Baton

Relay baton

The baton nobody drops in a handover, the moment where most hospital steps are lost.

Runs in with speed lines · passes itself hand to hand · spins to celebrate.

Object used elsewhere?
Clear. No baton mascot found.
Name risk
High. “I-PASS the BATON” is the standard clinical handoff mnemonic, and Baton was a Johns Hopkins-linked handoff-software startup. Baton AI (US) does workflow automation.
Watch
Familiar to clinicians, which helps recognition but makes the name impossible to own.

Sources: I-PASS the BATON · Baton AI

Good object, needs a new name; the plainest shape.

Maybe

A bookmark that keeps your place in each patient's journey.

Its two tails are its legs · the top folds over to bow · the tick on its chest lights up when done.

Object used elsewhere?
Clear. No bookmark mascot found; only read-later apps.

High. Nishaan also means scar (nishaan-e-zakhm), and Nishan Sahib is the Sikh holy flag.

Parchi

OPD slip

The paper slip every Indian patient carries from desk to desk, as a character that knows where to go next.

Gets a teal stamp when a step is done · rolls up to think · flutters between desks.

Object used elsewhere?
Clear. No prescription-slip character found; pharma mascots are blobs and organs.
Name risk
Medium. Parchaa is a Delhi healthtech with hospital queue modules (unverified page). “Parchi” is also the exam cheat-chit.
Watch
The paper slip is what Hospital OS replaces, so celebrating it sends a mixed message.

Sources: Parchi as cheat chit

Very Indian-hospital, but celebrates the paper you want to remove.

Drop

Gaanth

Knotted cloth potli

A cloth bundle tied with a reminder knot.

Knot ends perk, droop and curl into a “?” · loosens its knot to present.

Object used elsewhere?
Clear. No knotted-bundle mascot found.
Name risk
High. गाँठ also means a lump or tumour, which patients will hear in a hospital. Idioms link it to misused money, and “Gaanth” is a 2024 crime series about the Burari deaths.
Watch
The knot idea could survive under another name, but the story depends on the word.

Sources: lump meaning · Gaanth series

The lump meaning rules it out for hospitals.

Drop

Dabba

Steel tiffin

Three tiers for three pillars, delivered like the dabbawalas deliver lunch.

Tiers slide open to show modules · lid pops to celebrate.

Object used elsewhere?
Clear. No tiffin character; dabbawalas appear in ads as people.
Name risk
High. “Dabba trading” is illegal stock trading (NSE advisory, July 2026), and “dabba” is slang for junk. Dabba by Wonder and Wifi Dabba use the name.
Watch
Food and delivery cliché, with no link to care.

Sources: Dabba trading · Dabba by Wonder

Name carries illegal-trading and junk meanings.

Political symbol.

If you keep the sticky note: names to check

You liked the note. The object is open, but “Nudge” belongs to an AI scribe and billing-audit company. These are starting points for a trademark and meaning check, not cleared names.

YaadiFrom yaad, memory; a yaadi is a list. Says “I remember” in Hindi and Marathi.
TikkuFrom “tick”, in the style of an affectionate Hindi nickname. Says done.
ChipkuHindi slang for something that sticks to you. Playful; may read as clingy.
PinnuThe note pinned until done. Friendly, pan-Indian.

Each still needs: a trademark search in India (classes 9, 42 and 44), a check of app stores and health startups, and a read by speakers of the main regional languages.

My recommendation

Take three objects forward: the sticky note (your favourite), the letter and the thread spool. All three are open as objects and carry the follow-through story; only the letter's name is low risk as it stands. Drop the potli, tiffin, compass and lantern because of their names or symbols.

  1. Which objects go forward? I suggest note, letter and spool.
  2. Should I prototype them fully (all poses, in use on the site and social posts) like the last round?
  3. Do you want a naming round with a trademark check before or after the art?

The SVG for each option is saved in mascot/options/. Research covered the open web on 14 October 2026; absence of a match means none was found, not that none exists, and a formal trademark search is still needed.
